title: Enforcement Rules of the Salt Industry Cooperative Act — Attached Table and Source Supplements
full_text:
ENFORCEMENT RULES OF THE SALT INDUSTRY COOPERATIVE ACT [Attached Table]

DETAILED CRITERIA FOR SUSPENSION OF OPERATIONS
(Related to Article 2)

1. General criteria

(a) Where there are two or more violations, the period prescribed by the more severe sanction criterion shall be increased by up to one half of that period, without exceeding the sum of the periods prescribed by the respective sanction criteria.

(b) The administrative sanction criteria based on the number of violations apply where an administrative sanction has been imposed for the same violation within the preceding one year. The period shall be calculated by reference to the date on which the administrative sanction for the violation was imposed and the date on which the same violation, committed again after that sanction, was detected.

(c) The authority imposing the sanction may reduce the period of suspension of operations prescribed by the individual criteria in paragraph 2 by up to one half where any of the following applies:
1) The violation is recognized as having resulted from minor negligence or error;
2) The state of violation has been corrected or eliminated;
3) A reduction in the period of suspension of operations is otherwise deemed necessary, taking into account the seriousness of the violation, its motive, its consequences, and other relevant circumstances.

(d) A suspension of operations under paragraph 2 shall be limited to operations in the field related to the violation concerned.

2. Individual criteria

| Violation | Statutory basis | First violation | Second or subsequent violation |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Failure to comply with a corrective order under the introductory part of Article 51(1) of the Act | Article 51(2) of the Act | Suspension of operations for 3 months | Suspension of operations for 6 months |
| (b) Failure to comply with a requirement to replace officers through a new election under Article 51(1)1 of the Act | Article 51(2) of the Act | Suspension of operations for 3 months | Suspension of operations for 6 months |
| (c) Failure to comply with a requirement to suspend the duties of officers under Article 51(1)1 of the Act | Article 51(2) of the Act | Suspension of operations for 2 months | Suspension of operations for 4 months |
| (d) Failure to comply with a requirement to dismiss employees under Article 51(1)2 of the Act | Article 51(2) of the Act | Suspension of operations for 2 months | Suspension of operations for 4 months |
| (e) Failure to comply with a requirement to suspend employees from office under Article 51(1)2 of the Act | Article 51(2) of the Act | Warning | Suspension of operations for 2 months |
| (f) Failure to comply with a requirement to reduce employees' pay under Article 51(1)2 of the Act | Article 51(2) of the Act | Warning | Suspension of operations for 1 month |

ENACTMENT TEXT

⊙ Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries No. 782
The ordinance enacting the Enforcement Rules of the Salt Industry Cooperative Act is hereby promulgated as follows.

February 5, 2026
Minister of Oceans and Fisheries (seal)

Ordinance Enacting the Enforcement Rules of the Salt Industry Cooperative Act

[Omitted because it is identical to the main text]

ADDENDA
These Rules shall enter into force on the date of their promulgation.

REASONS FOR ENACTMENT OR AMENDMENT

[Enactment]

◇ Reasons for enactment and principal contents

The Salt Industry Cooperative Act has been amended to allow the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries to suspend a salt industry cooperative's operations for a specified period not exceeding six months where the cooperative fails to comply with a corrective order or similar requirement issued by the Minister upon finding that its operations or accounting violate a statute, an administrative disposition under a statute, or similar requirements. In line with that amendment, these Rules prescribe detailed criteria for administrative sanctions, including provisions allowing a suspension of operations for three months for a first failure to comply with a corrective order and for six months for a second or subsequent such violation.

■ 염업조합법 시행규칙 [별표]                                                   


                                                                                  


  업무정지의 세부기준(제2조 관련)                                                 


                                                                                  


  1. 일반기준                                                                     


    가. 위반행위가 둘 이상인 경우에는 각 처분기준을 합산한 기간을 넘지 않는       


  범위에서 무거운 처분기준에 그 처분기준의 2분의 1 범위에서 가중한다.             


    나. 위반행위의 횟수에 따른 행정처분 기준은 최근 1년간 같은 위반행위로 행      


  정처분을 받은 경우에 적용한다. 이 경우 기간의 계산은 위반행위에 대한            


  행정처분을 받은 날과 그 처분 후 다시 같은 위반행위를 하여 적발된 날을           


  기준으로 한다.                                                                  


    다. 처분권자는 다음의 어느 하나에 해당하는 경우에는 제2호의 개별기준에        


  따른 업무정지 기간의 2분의 1 범위에서 그 기간을 줄일 수 있다.                   


      1) 위반행위가 사소한 부주의나 오류로 인한 것으로 인정되는 경우              


      2) 위반상태를 시정하거나 해소한 경우                                        


      3) 그 밖에 위반행위의 정도, 위반행위의 동기와 그 결과 등을 고려하여 업      


  무정지 기간을 줄일 필요가 있다고 인정되는 경우                                  


    라. 제2호에 따른 업무정지 처분은 해당 위반행위 관련 분야 업무에 한정한다.     


                                                                                  


  2. 개별기준

SOURCE_SUPPLEMENT_REASON_2026020500782.source_quote:
[제정]


◇ 제정이유 및 주요내용


  염업조합의 업무와 회계가 법령, 법령에 따른 행정처분 등에 위반된다고 인정될 때 해양수산부장관이 명하는 시정명령 등을 염업조합이 이행하지 않은 경우에는 6개월 이내의 기간을 정하여 염업조합의 업무를 정지시킬 수 있도록 하는 내용으로 「염업조합법」이 개정된 것에 맞추어, 염업조합이 시정명령을 이행하지 않은 경우에는 1차 위반 시 3개월의 업무정지 처분을, 2차 이상 위반 시 6개월의 업무정지 처분을 각각 명할 수 있도록 하는 등 행정처분의 세부기준을 정하려는 것임.
